title: Review of ringswim SIBMD (C:swim-divide) on fresh seed 3: replicated with the author's tracker (72 persistent splits, generation 12, 63 ringed swimmers, 3 lineages that swim >= 3 BL ringed and divide; #385 swims 6.3 BL and divides into a ringed swimmer and a small end piece), but labkit's 1000-t lineage window finds only 2 persistent splits, as on the author's own packs
summary: labkit re-run of world.py on fresh seed 3 (pack/, 256^2, t=10000). From smoothed noise everywhere (sheet t=0), 25-99 walled cells settle to 33. L is membrane-like in aggregate (rim/core 1.64, rim/outside 5.45, 159/205 individually), and 72 long-lived tracks move >= 1 body length (max 4.5). labkit counts 336 splits but only 2 persistent splits (generation 2), with 260 merges (merge/split 0.77); the author's packs give 0-2 on seeds 0-2 as well. The author's ringtrack.py (contour-distance ring score; persistent split = 2 children that survive 400 t without merging) on seed 3 to t=20000 gives a ring >= 1.5 in 99.9% of 25806 cell-frames (median 2.01), 72 persistent splits, max generation 12, 206 splits / 172 merges, 63 tracks >= 3 BL (all ringed), and 3 lineages that swim >= 3 BL ringed and divide (rt256_s3.report.txt). Track #385 (generation 8): a ringed crescent (ring 1.83-2.01) swims 125 px (6.3 BL) from t=9540 and pinches at t~13100. Daughter #515 keeps the ring (1.68-2.09) and swims 121 px (6.3 BL); daughter #514 is a small round end piece (ring 1.74-2.35, moves 0.7 BL) (strip_s3_385.png, div_s3_385.png). Construction: L is made only inside cells (prodL = b K S, with K autocatalytic only where phi > 0 and phi^2-gated), so the chi ring is the cell's own product. The drive is the label-average phoretic drift of c07's established ringswim (each segmented body moves rigidly up its mean substrate gradient).

seeds_run.result: pass with the author's tracker; labkit's default lineage window gives 2 persistent splits (generation 2)

verdicts.limitation: D depends on the persistence window. With labkit's K=1000 t, persistent splits are 2 on my seed (0-2 on the author's), and with ringtrack's 400 t hold they are 72. Daughters mostly lose their identity in collisions or merges within ~1000 t (merges 0.77-0.83 of splits, a reticulate genealogy, so confidence is capped at medium). The joint B+M+D lineage I checked divides unequally: the swimming daughter carries most of the cell and the other is a small end piece. M comes from a per-body label-average drive (designed, nonlocal). I did not run the chi=0 or mu=0 controls, a resolution test or a Laplacian-only twin.
